title: Grateful Dead Live at Pirates World on 1970-03-24
lineage: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT (44.1k) > Sony R500 > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude v8.01 Professional > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a fire‑filled 1970 Pirates World show with a cosmic Dark Star, killer Good Lovin' jam and tight transitions.
ai_review.review: The recording is an excellent SBD/matrix mix – clear, well balanced and only marred by a splice in Dark Star and a missing intro to Morning Dew. Musically the show is a showcase of early‑70s energy: a soaring Dark Star, incendiary Don't Ease Me In, a monster Good Lovin', and a tight High Time > Dark Star > The Other One sequence that keeps fans dancing from start to finish.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (≥20, mostly 5‑star) praise both performance and sound quality; recording is described as crisp/excellent and the show is highlighted as one of the era’s best.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear, well‑balanced SBD with a slight splice in Dark Star and the first few seconds of Morning Dew missing; occasional vintage hiss but overall crisp and immersive.

standout_songs: High Time > Dark Star > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: Tight transitions (e.g., Lovelight into Uncle), high energy throughout, short but inspired jams that keep the momentum flowing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for blazing guitar leads, perfect tone on Dark Star and High Time, emotive vocals on Cold Rain/High Time, and dueling guitars with Bob on Morning Dew.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for bass work that sometimes sounds like a different instrument during Dark Star; overall solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for dueling guitar moments with Jerry, especially in the Morning Dew jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ praised as “in command” and a key driver of Good Lovin' and Lovelight jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Described as tight, machine‑gun/locomotive power; drum solo appropriate and not overly long.
